status: Timing semantics and conditional affine arithmetic; no event policy or clock chosen
value_lineage: C-15/P-29 requires causal context prediction and C-29/P-69 requires explicit frame transitions. C-24/P-52 preserves meaningful response timing; transport batching is not a license to change the observed sequence.

clocks.token_order: Ordered observations and the prefix available before each observation.
clocks.modeled_time: Elapsed model time controlling the specified response/noise/dynamics semantics.
clocks.neural_frame: Complete source/destination state transition at the chosen modeled interval.
clocks.learning_exposure: Which observed event or elapsed interval triggers an update; not automatically every neural frame.
clocks.wall_execution: CPU/transport execution time. It need not equal modeled time during offline design comparisons.

order_loss.condition: If a batch is reduced to a commutative aggregate and all other causally relevant state, parameters and future forcing are identical, permutations of that batch cannot be distinguished later by that model.
order_loss.scope: The condition excludes order-dependent retained state or ordered parameter updates. It does not assert that all batching loses order.
order_loss.general_difference: For two affine updates with identity input injection, x_AB-x_BA=(W-I)*(u_A-u_B).
order_loss.exact_linear_batch: For m ordered inputs, x_m=W^m*x_0+sum_(j=0..m-1) W^(m-1-j)*u_j. The positional factors preserve ordering; replacing this with an unweighted sum generally does not.
order_loss.limits: The reference has no cancellation, transfer nonlinearity, quantization, learning or noise. The exact affine formula does not justify collapsing actual nonlinear completed frames.

boundary_alignment.observation: Distinct events may map to the same frame boundary. Ordering them afterward or spreading them across boundaries is an explicit processing/time choice, not an unordered sum.
boundary_alignment.pure_decay_bound: For a reference exponential with half-life H, an age shift less than Delta changes the amplitude ratio by at most1-2^(-Delta/H). This bounds isolated decay only.
boundary_alignment.limits: The delay bound assumes independent boundary alignment with no queue backlog. Threshold, cancellation, recurrence, prediction windows and batched service can have different or larger consequences; no acceptable Delta follows from the scalar bound.

event_vs_time_decay.equation: If an event-indexed mode retains r per observation, physical-time half-life at regular event gap T is T*ln(1/2)/ln(r).
event_vs_time_decay.observation: One learning exposure per token does not make neural evolution event-clocked. A fixed per-event recurrence changes physical duration as token pacing changes.
event_vs_time_decay.limits: Pure scalar decay can use time-dependent retention; this does not supply a valid arbitrary-time root of a learned nonlinear or discrete transition.

prediction_boundary.before: Assess prediction available from the complete causal state and parameters before the observed token or its teaching update changes them.
prediction_boundary.after: Use the now-observed token for independently defined learning responsibility and any justified state intervention, respecting H-84 generation exclusion.
prediction_boundary.between: Specify how the preceding observed prefix becomes available to predict the next token. Merely applying several learning updates to one unchanged neural frame does not establish this.
prediction_boundary.alternatives: Frame-aligned ordered observations and explicitly ordered within-interval input handling can be compared. H-75 alone does not select one token per frame, require a persistent token buffer, or authorize partial-frame recurrent reads.
prediction_boundary.future_information: A supplied sequence identity, expected continuation or position label contains information beyond an otherwise ambiguous observed prefix. Such a cue must be an explicit task input, not silently borrowed from the training record to claim history-based disambiguation.

future_comparisons.alternatives: Ordered frame-aligned presentation versus explicitly ordered input handling within a modeled interval
future_comparisons.observations: Prefix-sensitive pre-input predictions, preservation of token order, actual modeled spacing and neural work; identical packet batching must not silently redefine the sequence.

future_comparisons.alternatives: Several event spacings at a stated neural time resolution
future_comparisons.observations: Prediction availability, useful history, dominant fading and exposure count; distinguish order recognition from learning exact duration.

future_comparisons.alternatives: Information-equivalent initial contexts versus an explicitly supplied external start cue
future_comparisons.observations: What the model actually knows before each prediction; no hidden sequence labels, future tokens or position labels in the prediction readout.

scope_limit: Exact finite affine composition and scalar time arithmetic only. No SNN implementation/training, neural simulation, benchmark, project tests or build.
